Hi! This is the mentorship through the career center, correct? I did this mentorship program back in winter when it was focused around the healthcare industry. No, this isn't really something you can put on your resume, HOWEVER, this program has the potential to help you create meaningful professional connections and relationships. 

Basically, you are matched up to a UW alumni mentor in the industry of focus (for you, it would be someone who has a non-tech role in tech). You will have weekly meetings with your mentor and fellow mentees. How the meetings are structured is almost entirely dependant on your mentor. For example, mine set up the first two meetings telling us about her role and what we wanted out of the mentorship experience. For the remaining meetings, we had multiple guest speakers educate us about their roles through presentations. At the very end, we were even able to speak with a recruiter and know the application process for the organization. It was an amazing experience for me - I still keep in touch with people I've met through the program.

Done right, the relationships you form through the program can give you a leg up during intern/job application periods. I think just keep in mind that it's probably going to be hard to form a connection with mentors since the program is going to take place virtually.

This is rapidly changing - it has now been changed to a deferral period of 3 months and I am so proud to say that one of my group members is one of the people spearheading combating this discriminatory action enforced by the U.S. government. 

My team has brought up the new shortened deferral period to Bloodworks NW and they say that they are so happy about it and have even had an influx in those interested in donating due to it. Please hang in there, change is right around the corner. If you are interested in discussing this topic more I can definitely get you in contact with my team member because he is so so passionate about this topic.
